newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares recover from weaker opening.
newsitem.headline: French shares recover from weaker opening.

text.p: French shares opened weaker then bounced into positive territory as Japan moved to reassure financial markets over remarks from Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto that had sent Wall Street tumbling overnight.
The CAC-40 blue-chip share index recovered to trade 6.52 points or 0.24 percent higher at 2,768.72 points after opening down 0.49 percent in the wake of Wall Street's second biggest one-day loss.
New York's late sell-off on Monday was ignited by Hashimoto's comments that stable exchange rates were critical to Japan's continued buying of U.S. government securities.

"I hope the U.S. will engage in efforts and in cooperation to maintain exchange stability so we will not succumb to the temptation to sell off Treasury bills and switch our funds to gold," Hashimoto said.
But Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters in Japan on Tuesday that Japan had not sold U.S. Treasuries and had no intention of doing so.
He also said Hashimoto's "real intention" concerning investments in U.S. Treasuries had been incorrectly reported.
Those remarks, coming a few minutes into the French trading day, wiped out opening index losses which had already been muted by earlier Japanese attempts overnight to prevent market panic.

State-controlled French bank Credit Lyonnais was among the biggest early gainers with a 4.50 percent jump after a newspaper report that it expects a two billion franc profit for 1997 after a cost-cutting programme.
